classification.difficultyReason: Combine two elevation triangles with a right angle inferred from bearings to determine an unknown height.

content.prompt: From a point $A$, a lighthouse is on a bearing of $026^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and the top of the lighthouse is at angle of elevation of $20.5^{\circ}$. From a point $B$, the lighthouse is on a bearing of $296^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and the top of the lighthouse is at angle of elevation of $10.2^{\circ}$. If $A$ and $B$ are 500 metres apart, find the height of the lighthouse, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.short:
$81\text{ m}$

Use the bearings to identify a right-angled ground triangle, then combine Pythagoras’ theorem with the two tangent ratios.
answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the foot of the lighthouse, $T$ its top and $OT=h$ metres. The reverse bearings of $A$ and $B$ from $O$ are $206^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and $116^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle AOB=90^{\circ}$.

In the vertical right-angled triangles:
$$\begin{align*}\tan20.5^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{OA}\\OA&=\frac{h}{\tan20.5^{\circ}}\\\tan10.2^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{OB}\\OB&=\frac{h}{\tan10.2^{\circ}}\end{align*}$$
Applying Pythagoras’ theorem to the horizontal triangle $AOB$:
$$\begin{align*}OA^2+OB^2&=500^2\\\left(\frac{h}{\tan20.5^{\circ}}\right)^2+\left(\frac{h}{\tan10.2^{\circ}}\right)^2&=250000\\h^2\left(\frac{1}{\tan^220.5^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan^210.2^{\circ}}\right)&=250000\\h&=\frac{500}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\tan^220.5^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan^210.2^{\circ}}}}\\h&\approx81.0655\end{align*}$$
The lighthouse is $81\text{ m}$ high, correct to the nearest metre.
